patterns.title: Flag & Pole breakout
patterns.idea: A sharp advance (the pole), then a shallow drift against it on falling volume (the flag), then a close back through the flag's high. The measured move projects the pole from the breakout.

patterns.title: Consolidation breakout (rectangle / Darvas box)
patterns.idea: Price oscillates between a flat ceiling and a floor, is rejected at the same level repeatedly, then closes through it. The ceiling is real supply; clearing it means that supply is finished.

patterns.title: Consolidation, before the breakout (early base)
patterns.idea: The only screen here that does not wait for a breakout. A stock already in an uptrend, pausing under a flat ceiling with its EMAs bunched and its range and volume drying up, EARLY in the sequence of bases since it reclaimed the 200 EMA -- so the setup is visible while price is still inside the range rather than on the day it leaves.

patterns.title: 52-week high breakout
patterns.idea: A close above the highest HIGH of the past year, after a real absence from that level. Not a shape -- an anchoring effect: investors treat the old high as a ceiling and under-react when it is cleared.

leadership.note: RS Rating is IBD-style: 12-month performance weighted 40% to the latest quarter (0.4 x 3M + 0.2 x 6M + 0.2 x 9M + 0.2 x 12M), ranked 1-99 across every stock with a full year of prices, then filtered -- so 90 means it beat 90% of the market whatever floor is set. Liquid = median traded value over 50 sessions at or above the floor; a stock with no volume data fails it. Prices are price-return (no dividends).
